# Jarvis ### Your intelligence. Your hardware. A private, local-first AI assistant with voice and text chat.
Talk naturally, as if Jarvis were a third person in the room. **Voice-first · Local AI · Personal memory · No subscription** [**Download Jarvis →**](https://github.com/isair/jarvis/releases)   ·   [Website](https://barissencan.com/jarvis/)   ·   [Get started](#quick-install)   ·   [Explore the app](#inside-jarvis)   ·   [Support the project](#support)
--- ## An assistant that lives with you, not in the cloud Jarvis is built to be part of the conversation. Talk through an idea, discuss plans with a friend, then ask “Jarvis, what do you think?” While listening, it keeps a short, temporary rolling transcript of nearby speech so it can join an ongoing conversation using what was just discussed. Your diary and knowledge graph stay on your computer. Speech and chat models run locally when you use a local model server. A voice, a face, and a place in the conversation.

candidates.description: Playwright MCP server built to cut agent turns and tokens: one-call form filling, delta snapshots, batched steps, and a submit guard on by default
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# turbo-browser-mcp

[![CI](https://github.com/Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Tthanh2k6/turbo-browser-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/turbo-browser-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/turbo-browser-mcp)
![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-brightgreen)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)

An MCP server for browser automation, built on Playwright. It has 11 tools, and each one does more per call than the usual one-action-per-call design:

- `smart_fill_form` fills a whole form in one call, including React inputs, selects, comboboxes, rich-text editors and file uploads read from disk.
- `inspect_compact` can return only the elements that changed since the last snapshot.
- `batch_actions` runs a list of clicks, key presses, form steps and page reads as one call.

Fewer calls means fewer model turns and less page text replayed in the conversation. The numbers, and their limits, are under [Benchmarks](#benchmarks).

Buttons that look like a final commit (Submit, Send, Publish, Pay, Confirm, and their Korean, Japanese, Chinese and Vietnamese equivalents) are blocked by default, so an agent can prefill a form and leave the last click to a person. Pass `allowSubmit: true` per call or start with `--allow-submit` to turn this off.

The server does not hide that the browser is automated: no stealth patches, no fingerprint changes, no CAPTCHA solving. For sites with a bot check it can hand the tab to a person and continue afterwards ([`wait_for_human`](#handing-a-step-to-a-person-wait_for_human---open-profile)).

## Install

Needs Node 20 or newer and a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Brave, or Playwright's Chromium).

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add turbo-browser -- npx -y turbo-browser-mcp
```

Clients that read an `mcpServers` JSON config (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Antigravity and others):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "turbo-browser": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "turbo-browser-mcp"],
      "env": { "TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT": "/absolute/path/to/workspace" }
    }
  }
}
```

`TURBO_BROWSER_SAVE_ROOT` is the only folder the server may write screenshots, PDFs and storage files to, or read storage files from. Leave it out and the current working directory is used.

Check the setup, and install Chromium if no browser is found:

```bash
npx -y turbo-browser-mcp --doctor
npx playwright-core install chromium
```

n8n-MCP is an open-source MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other AI assistants operate n8n: read failed executions, edit workflows in place, validate and test them, manage credentials, and build new workflows. It works with any n8n instance that has the Public API enabled, and can use n8n's built-in MCP server as a second backend.

## What You Can Do With It

- **Debug failing workflows** - `n8n_executions` reads an execution and, with `mode: "error"`, returns the error, the failing node, and sample items from the node before it.
- **Edit workflows in place** - `n8n_update_partial_workflow` applies targeted operations to the nodes and connections named in the request, so the assistant does not resend the whole workflow. This includes find-and-replace inside one large field such as a Code node (`patchNodeField`). By default n8n-MCP saves a snapshot before it changes a workflow's nodes or connections, and `n8n_workflow_versions` can diff and roll back.
- **Validate and fix before going live** - `validate_node`, `validate_workflow`, and `n8n_validate_workflow` report unknown nodes, invalid node versions, missing required fields, and broken connections or expressions. `n8n_autofix_workflow` repairs the common ones.

# I Spent 4,500+ Hours Coding with AI. This Is the Claude Code Setup I Ended Up With.

> *The engineering instructions, curated skills, and three-stage review workflow I use to keep AI-assisted development fast, controlled, and verifiable.*

---

## Table of Contents

- [1. The Story Behind This Setup](#1-the-story-behind-this-setup)
- [2. Core Engineering Philosophy](#2-core-engineering-philosophy)
- [3. The Three-Prompt Review Workflow](#3-the-three-prompt-review-workflow)
- [4. Curated Skills & Upstream Attribution](#4-curated-skills--upstream-attribution)
  - [Superpowers (Jesse Vincent)](#superpowers)
  - [Ponytail (Dietrich Gebert)](#ponytail)
  - [I Have ADHD (ayghri)](#i-have-adhd)
- [5. Repository Structure](#5-repository-structure)
- [6. Adoption Guide](#6-adoption-guide)
- [7. Credits](#7-credits)

---

## 1. The Story Behind This Setup

This repository is not a speculative prompt collection.

It is the setup I arrived at after spending an estimated **4,500+ hours** actively building, debugging, refactoring, and deploying software alongside AI coding agents.

> [!NOTE]
> *The 4,500+ hours figure is a personal working estimate based on roughly six productive hours per day over a little more than two years of daily engineering work. It is not tracked automated telemetry.*

### The Tooling Journey
My day-to-day workflow evolved across multiple waves of AI developer tooling:
- **Cursor** for inline completions and multi-file agent edits.
- **Claude Code CLI** for autonomous terminal-driven task loops and micro-diff inspections.
- **Antigravity IDE & Gemini CLI** for multi-agent workflows, skill architectures, and background automations.
- **Codex, OpenCode, and Amazon Q**, exploring how different models reason about API contracts, context limits, and tool-calling.

I do not claim equal usage across all these platforms. What became clear through thousands of hours across all of them was a universal pattern:

> **Unconstrained AI coding agents fail predictably.**  
> They suffer from confirmation bias, over-engineer simple utilities into speculative generic frameworks, write code against hallucinated APIs, quietly reformat adjacent files, and declare "tests pass!" without actually executing them.

This repository represents the guardrails, prompts, and behavioral directives I built to reduce those failure modes. It is a practical, personal setup designed for real production work.

It includes everything you need to go from early prototypes to production-ready applications. Mastra integrates with frontend and backend frameworks like React, Next.js, and Node, or you can deploy it anywhere as a standalone server. It's the easiest way to build, tune, and scale reliable AI products.

Purpose-built for TypeScript and designed around established AI patterns, Mastra gives you everything you need to build great AI applications out-of-the-box.

- [**Agents**](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview): Build autonomous agents that use LLMs and tools to solve open-ended tasks. Agents reason about goals, decide which tools to use, and iterate internally until the model emits a final answer or an optional stopping condition is met.
